title: Growing Number of Apps Help Adults Make Friends
paragraphs: Making friends as an adult can be hard. You might meet someone nice through work or a hobby, but later you find that you don't have much in common, or you have opposite schedules.
So why not let an algorithm decide your friends for you?
A growing number of online platforms are doing just that — or at least, letting people meet possible new friends in their area.

In the UK, for example, there's a website called People Like You (PLY). You tell it things like your job and your interests, and then it matches you with a small group of people, and presents a list of regular events where you can meet.
You might go for drinks, or try bowling, hiking, or going to a comedy club. If you meet someone you like, you can invite them to join you at the next event.

The platform isn't free to use, though — there are different membership options, starting at about $13.50 a month. However, this also covers the cost of the first activity, such as a movie ticket or the fee for a cooking class — though if you're going out for dinner, you still have to pay for your own food.
The people who run the platform believe that having to pay to use it encourages people to actually meet up, rather than just signing up and staying home.
"When you do things for free, people often don't turn up," PLY founder Karen Harris told The Guardian.
You can also pay to just join a single event. But Harris says that, on average, it takes three events to find "your person."
Another platform called Agora works in a similar way. Agora says that, in its first two years, it has held over 300 events in London, and helped form over 400 friendships.
